page: Amazon Web Services r6id.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized compute instance driven by two Intel Xeon 8375C processors running on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled at 3.5 GHz. Backing this compute density is 1024 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Unlike virtualized instances, the bare-metal architecture grants direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead, supported by 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and 7600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark measurements highlight strong multi-threaded capabilities and sustained I/O throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in PassMark CPU score (88,191.68), cryptographic tests (115,184.78), and extended vector instructions. Multi-core compute evaluations in Geekbench and stress-ng register in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is substantial, reaching 338.87 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 132.33 GB/sec for uncached writes. Conversely, single-core metrics across Geekbench and stress-ng place in the middle 50 percent, reflecting standard per-core execution speeds typical of high-core-count enterprise server processors.

The inclusion of 7600 GB local NVMe SSD capacity and a large 1 TB memory footprint offers solid resource consolidation for dense data systems. In throughput tests, the hardware handles 110.69 million Redis SET operations per second and demonstrates strong database operation throughput. Workload tradeoffs center on resource scale: while highly efficient for concurrent processing and in-memory architectures, single-threaded applications do not extract maximum value from this massive core count.

Amazon Web Services r6id.metal is primarily suited for large enterprise relational databases, distributed in-memory data grids, Redis clusters, big data analytics, and high-concurrency Clang compilation pipelines requiring high memory allocations alongside low-latency local NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r6id.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by 64-core, 128-thread Intel Xeon 8375C processors clocked at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 1024 GB of DDR4 memory at a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 50 Gbps network bandwidth, it provides high hardware density without hypervisor overhead. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute and cryptographic performance, accompanied by high memory bandwidth exceeding 338 GB/sec for uncached reads. Single-thread performance remains average, indicating that performance gains stem from massive parallelization rather than single-core frequency. In-memory operations show high throughput, sustaining over 110 million Redis SET operations per second. The server is well matched for memory-intensive enterprise databases, Redis or Memcached clusters, big data analytics engines, and high-throughput transaction processing systems that require low-latency local storage and substantial physical memory.
